subject: Retroactive capacity spike and commit extension request
messages:
From: Megan Clark <megan@olivelabs.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@olivelabs.com
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Retroactive capacity spike: Jan-Mar usage reconciliation

Hi Mateo,

Hope you’re well. We finished our internal audit for Q1 and found a significant backlog of inference demand that landed against our Redwood Dedicated pool between Jan 10 and Mar 28 — roughly 18M extra tokens above our committed baseline. We expected transient spikes but those were captured after our renewal window and are showing as overage on the March invoice.

Attached is our usage export (olivelabs_usage_Q1.csv) and a short summary from our ops team. Can Redwood help reconcile this so we can close our quarter? Specifically: 1) we need a one-off true-up amount for the retrospective consumption, and 2) we'd like to explore adding more committed capacity for the remainder of our term rather than repeating overage payments.

Our procurement team wants a formal quote/PO-friendly document and a clear payment timeline. Can you advise next steps?

Thanks,
Megan Clark
Billing & Finance Lead
Olive Labs

On Fri, Apr 01, 2027 at 15:02, Operations <ops@olivelabs.com> wrote:
> Attached export shows token counts per day; spike correlates with a model rollout we did in mid-Jan.

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Megan Clark <megan@olivelabs.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retroactive capacity spike: Jan-Mar usage reconciliation

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear data. I reviewed the CSV and ran it against our billing logs. Short summary: the extra 18M tokens falls into three cluster windows tied to higher concurrency and a longer average sequence length after your Jan rollout. We can handle this two ways:

Option A — One-time true-up: invoice the retrospective consumption at your current overage rate; our estimate is $32,400 for the period. Payment terms Net 30.

Option B — Commit extension + amortized credit: add a 6-month incremental commitment that buys down the true-up by 40% (applied as monthly credits across the new commitment). You’d get predictable unit economics going forward and avoid a large lump payment.

I attached our working breakdown (redwood_review_Q1_breakdown.pdf) — it shows per-window token counts, how we applied your baseline, and the math for the two options. If you want, we can join procurement and ops on a quick call tomorrow to walk through.

If procurement prefers a formal quote, Ben in finance will produce a PO-ready PDF and DocuSign link after you confirm which option you prefer.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive — Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Megan Clark <megan@olivelabs.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@olivelabs.com
Date: 2027-05-03T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retroactive capacity spike: Jan-Mar usage reconciliation

Mateo,

Thanks — Option B sounds preferable if the amortization schedule is explicit and we can see the monthly credit amounts reflected on invoices. Our legal is also asking for two items before we sign anything: 1) a short note confirming this true-up will not count as a penalty and 2) payment terms options (Net 30 vs Net 60). Procurement wants the PO to match the DocuSign quote exactly.

Can Ben generate the PO-ready quote and include an amortization table and the proposed effective dates for the commit extension?

Megan
Billing & Finance Lead
Olive Labs

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Megan Clark <megan@olivelabs.com>, mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-05T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: OL — True-up quote and DocuSign link

Hi Megan / Mateo,

Attached is the PO-ready quote (OL-TrueUp-Quote-323400.pdf) and a DocuSign link for Option B (commit extension + amortized credit): https://docusign.com/OL-TrueUp-4571.

Key terms in the quote:
- One-time assessed consumption: $32,340 (matches breakdown)
- Amortization: 40% credit applied over 6 months to new incremental commit, resulting in a $12,936 credit spread monthly across months 1–6 following effective date.
- Payment terms: standard Net 30. We can offer Net 60 with a 1% early-payment credit if your AP team needs more runway.

If you confirm Option B, we’ll update the contract term to add 6 months to the current commitment term (effective on the DocuSign signature date) and issue a revised invoice template that shows the monthly credit lines for transparency.

Ben Carter
Senior Finance Manager, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OL-TrueUp-Quote-323400.pdf
From: Megan Clark <megan@olivelabs.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@olivelabs.com
Date: 2027-05-09T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OL — True-up quote and DocuSign link

Ben / Mateo — we’ve reviewed the quote with Procurement and Legal. We’ll proceed with Option B. Procurement will issue a PO to match the DocuSign quote and route it for signature this week.

Two small asks before signature: please make sure the DocuSign copies the amortization table into the line-item notes and add a short contractual clause that this true-up is an agreed reconciliation (non-punitive). Otherwise procurement is ready to move.

I’ll forward the PO when it’s issued. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

— Megan
Megan Clark
Billing & Finance Lead
Olive Labs
